Draft rules on cyber incident reporting for operators of essential services

Status: Consultation open until 30 November 2026

Published 14 September 2026 by the Office of Fixture Regulation. Reference OFR/2026/017.

The Office of Fixture Regulation is consulting on draft rules that set out how operators of essential services report significant cyber incidents. The rules apply to operators in the energy, transport, health, drinking water and digital infrastructure sectors that are designated under the Network Security Act.

An incident is significant when it causes, or is capable of causing, severe disruption of an essential service or financial loss for the operator, or when it affects other people by causing considerable material or non-material damage. The draft rules list the factors an operator weighs, including the number of users affected, the duration of the disruption and the geographical area concerned.

Under the draft rules an operator sends an early warning within 24 hours of becoming aware of a significant incident. A full incident notification follows within 72 hours. It updates the early warning and gives an initial assessment of the incident, its severity and impact, and any indicators of compromise. A final report is due within one month of the notification.

Operators that rely on a cloud provider or managed service provider remain responsible for reporting. The draft rules require contracts with such providers to oblige the provider to inform the operator of incidents without undue delay, so that the operator can meet its own deadlines.

The Office will publish a reporting template and a secure online form before the rules take effect. Reports may also be made through the national computer security incident response team, which will forward them to the Office within one working day.

Responses to this consultation should explain whether the thresholds are clear, whether the deadlines are workable for small operators, and whether the draft rules duplicate obligations that operators already have under data protection law.

How to respond

Send responses by email to consultations@regulator.example.invalid or by post to the address on our contact page.
